concept.name: Exchange outflow
concept.definition: Exchange outflow is the volume of coins withdrawn on-chain from exchange-attributed wallets over a period, commonly read as accumulation or movement to self-custody and reduced immediate sell pressure.
concept.intuition: Coins leaving the exchange are goods carried home from the market — they are being put back into storage rather than offered for sale.
concept.mechanics: Analytics providers sum transfers out of labeled exchange wallets; sustained net outflow shrinks exchange balances (reserves). After the March 2020 crash, outflow declined more slowly than inflow, so net flow stayed negative and the total BTC balance on exchanges dropped ~7% from its February high — a classic accumulation signature.
concept.formula: Net exchange flow = inflow − outflow; negative net flow = reserves shrinking.
concept.failure_modes: Outflows to new exchange wallets or institutional custodians can be misread as self-custody accumulation; reserve decline can also reflect an exchange losing customers (a red flag, not bullishness) — context matters.
concept.misconceptions: Outflow is not proof of buying — coins bought OTC or already held can simply be withdrawn, and a single whale reshuffling custody distorts daily figures. Persistent trends over weeks carry far more signal than one-day spikes.
concept.example: In mid-2020, BTC exchange outflows persistently exceeded inflows at 50-100k BTC per month rates in later Glassnode reporting, draining exchange balances as post-crash accumulators moved coins to cold storage.

citations.source: Glassnode Insights - The Number of BTC On Exchanges Is Down Almost 7%
